  "messages": [
    {
      "id": "msg_1e5d8e6a3001Ljp81nv9w2g8Ys",
      "metadata": {
        "displayText": "you're working on sinjoh. read the project documentation to familiarize yourself first. you'll also need to get familiar with kohjoh, pokeplatinum (the original source), pokeplatinum-3ds (the existing new3ds-only port), and coffeepot. we are going to take a very different route. you are going to bootstrap an entirely new source port of pokemon platinum, as a nintendo 3ds homebrew. your end goal is to replicate all of the remaster enhancements of pokeplatinum-3ds, but based on kohjoh's more sane internals, and targeting the original 2011 3ds - not the 2015 new 3ds. some fancy things like scaling might be too much for the original 3ds meager hardware, and that's okay. as it turns out, if we pre-compute wideart at compile/package time, wideart is cheap enough for o3ds - so you must include that too. your goal is to squeeze the remaster/port into the old3ds hardware, not to worry about new3ds enhancements. you only need to get sinjoh-platinum working, forget about sinjoh-diamond or sinjoh-pearl for now. most of the hard work, engineering and research has already been done for you. you should refer heavily to the reference material in the workdir. you will test your own work using an emulator - we had too much trouble with lotus, so you will stick to azahar. always cross reference with coffeepot or kohjoh's documentation. especially since we are going for remastered enhancements, you will need to use every hardware cheat in the book to make sure this runs stable on old 3ds. read docs/chatlog00 to see where the last agent left off - there's uncommitted work in the tree, and chatlog00 will detail a bunch of pitfalls that we've already ran into along the way. ",
        "comments": [],
        "attachments": [],

            "content": [
              {
                "type": "text",
                "text": "Read file C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\sinjoh\\README.md, lines 1-94\n1: # sinjoh\n2: \n3: A native Nintendo 3DS source port of **Pokémon Platinum**, built for the\n4: **original 2011 3DS** (and 2DS) at stock clock and 64 MB application memory.\n5: \n6: Sinjoh is a new runtime, not a fork of `pokeplatinum-3ds`. Its internals are\n7: **kohjoh's**: the HGSS Old-3DS port's single game-owned frame loop, GPU-native\n8: 2D tile atlas, object-space retained 3D with a PICA matrix palette, baked CPU\n9: lighting for stable lists, decoded-ADPCM cache, and conservative pacing. The\n10: game itself is the pinned `pret/pokeplatinum` decompilation, compiled for the\n11: 3DS's ARM11 against a NitroSDK compatibility layer, exactly as kohjoh compiles\n12: HeartGold.\n13: \n14: The target experience is the `pokeplatinum-3ds` remaster on hardware that\n15: project does not support:\n16: \n17: - both screens filled, native-resolution 3D at 400x240 on the top screen;\n18: - the widened field camera and layout (25% more world at the sides);\n19: - the lower screen as a menu in the field;\n20: - crisp GPU-rendered 2D from a tile atlas;\n21: - WideArt bands, **precomputed at package time** so O3DS only uploads them;\n22: - stable 30 Hz presentation, no interpolation, no stereo, no sun shadows,\n23:   no 2x2 supersampling, no xBRZ.\n24: \n25: Those exclusions are deliberate. The GPU is the same 268 MHz PICA200 on both\n26: models; the New 3DS's advantage is CPU and RAM. Sinjoh spends the O3DS budget\n27: on CPU work removed (retained geometry, atlas 2D, ADPCM cache) and keeps GPU\n28: work flat.\n29: \n30: ## Status\n31: \n32: Foundation. The engine is in place under `engine/`; the game source, the\n33: NitroSDK and NitroSystem decompilations bootstrap reproducibly; the LOTUS MCP\n34: harness drives windowed sessions. The game-side patch stack and the\n35: engine/game link are the current work (see `docs/STATUS.md`).\n36: \n37: Nothing here is certified on O3DS hardware. LOTUS and Azahar are integration\n38: debuggers, not timing authorities.\n39: \n40: ## Layout\n41: \n42: ```\n43: engine/        kohjoh's runtime and GPU renderer, adapted (GPL-3.0)\n44:   app/         entry, lifecycle, pacing\n45:   runtime/     the DS/3DS bridge, G3 interpreter, frame publisher\n46:   graphics/    g2d atlas, g3d retained geometry, textures, renderer\n47:   audio/       sound-chip host, mixer, ADPCM cache\n48:   content/     indexed data pack\n49:   storage/     save store\n50:   diagnostics/ perf ring, crash handler\n51: tools/\n52:   game/        bootstrap, source inventory, overlay map, build driver\n53:   lotus_mcp.py MCP client for windowed LOTUS\n54: wideart/       hand-drawn wide-view bands (no game pixels)\n55: patches/       sinjoh patch stacks (pokeplatinum, NitroSDK, NitroSystem)\n56: docs/          architecture, porting plan, LOTUS findings, provenance\n57: ```\n58: \n59: ## Build\n60: \n61: Prerequisites: devkitPro (`devkitARM`, `libctru`, `citro3d`, `3dstools`,\n62: `picasso`) and Git for Windows on PATH ahead of MSYS2's git.\n63: \n64: ```sh\n65: python tools/game/bootstrap.py        # pinned decomp + SDKs, apply patches\n66: make -f engine/game.mk TARGET=3ds program -j8\n67: ```\n68: \n69: The build writes `build/game/3ds/sinjoh.3dsx`. On Windows, run make from the\n70: devkitPro MSYS2 shell with Git for Windows first on `PATH` (its own git can\n71: fetch over HTTPS; MSYS2's cannot).\n72: \n73: The data pack needs the player's own Platinum dump, never committed:\n74: \n75: ```sh\n76: python builder/extract_rom.py path/to/platinum.nds --output build/data_pack\n77: python builder/pack.py build/data_pack -o build/platinum.pak --build-id platinum-nitrofs-1\n78: ```\n79: \n80: Stage `build/platinum.pak` and `build/data_pack/manifest.json` as\n81: `sdmc:/3ds/kohjoh/data/platinum.pak` and `platinum.manifest.json`.\n82: `pwsh tools/azahar/run.ps1 -Edition platinum -Pack ... -Manifest ...` does\n83: that and collects screenshots and the log.\n84: \n85: ## Provenance and licence\n86: \n87: Sinjoh's own code is GPL-3.0. The engine is adapted from\n88: [`kohjoh`](https://github.com/estyseesghosts/kohjoh) (GPL-3.0). The game-side\n89: compatibility work is derived from the patch stack of\n90: [`pokeplatinum-3ds`](https://github.com/GabeSud0/pokeplatinum-3ds) (GPL-3.0);\n91: its renderer is **not** imported. See `PROVENANCE.md` and `NOTICE.md`.\n92: \n93: No ROM, extracted asset, save or captured game image belongs in this\n94: repository or its artifacts."

Decision in brief\\n9: \\n10: **Do not translate DS graphics registers into equivalent 3DS graphics registers: there are no equivalents for most of the DS's 2D pipeline.** Retain the game's logical render state, translate that state into native scene descriptions, and submit well-batched PICA200 geometry. The renderer never rasterizes a single\n5: pixel on the CPU in the shipping path.\n6: \n7: ## Two halves, one bridge\n8: \n9: | Half | Compiled with | Contents |\n10: | --- | --- | --- |\n11: | DS side | NitroSDK types, 4-byte enums | `build/upstream` (game), `engine/runtime`, `engine/compat/nitro`, `engine/compat/nitrosystem` |\n12: | 3DS side | libctru/citro3d, short enums | `engine/app`, `engine/graphics`, `engine/audio`, `engine/content`, `engine/storage`, `engine/diagnostics` |\n13: \n14: They meet only at `engine/runtime/kj_bridge.h`: fixed-width types, plain\n15: structs, `kj_ds_*` implemented on the DS side and `kj_ctr_*` on the 3DS side.\n16: No enums cross the line, and no NitroSDK or libctru header is included there.\n17: The boundary is kohjoh's and is kept unchanged; sinjoh's work goes into what is\n18: on each side of it.\n19: \n20: ## Frame flow\n21: \n22: 1. The game's own main loop runs on the main thread (`kj_game_main`).\n23: 2. Every emulated DS V-blank (`OS_Halt`) calls `kj_ctr_vblank`: APT, input,\n24:    audio service, then a wait locked to the physical V-blank count. A late\n25:    frame does not wait, so the game never loses DS time against real-time\n26:    audio; a stall over 30 V-blanks resynchronises.\n27: 3. After the V-blank callback and vwait tasks, `engine/runtime/kj_frame.c` walks\n28:    any H-blank effect and publishes one coherent snapshot: registers, palettes,\n29:    OAM, VRAM banks, per-line registers and the last swapped 3D scene.\n30: 4. `engine/graphics/renderer.c` waits for the previous GPU frame, records both\n31:    screens and submits. Nothing reads DS memory after it returns. If the game\n32:    is two or more refreshes behind, the presentation is skipped and counted;\n33:    the game tick is not.\n34: \n35: There is one frame loop: the game's. O3DS is the design floor: the program\n36: never enables the New 3DS clock or L2, and it runs in the ordinary 64 MB\n37: application memory mode.\n38: \n39: Presentation is 30 Hz on O3DS by contract: the DS game ticks at 60 Hz, the\n40: renderer presents every second coherent frame, and a late frame is dropped\n41: rather than delaying the game. 60 Hz frame interpolation, if added, is an\n42: opt-in New 3DS enhancement with its own thread budget; it is not part of the\n43: O3DS baseline and must never consume O3DS memory or CPU.\n44: \n45: ## 2D\n46: \n47: DS tiles are palette-expanded into a 1024x1024 RGBA5551 atlas, one DS 8x8 tile\n48: per PICA tile. A slot is reused only when its tile bytes are byte-identical and\n49: its palette version unchanged: no write tracking, no hashing of VRAM. Layers\n50: draw in DS priority order, with the 3D scene at BG0's slot. Stencil bits carry\n51: blend-target membership and window regions; BLDY and master brightness are\n52: full-screen passes. Text-BG and OBJ layers are retained when their inputs\n53: (registers, palette, map/OAM, ext palettes, the character bytes read) are\n54: byte-identical; an unchanged screen is not redrawn or transferred.\n55: \n56: For sinjoh this is also the 2D remaster path: the top screen's 2D is drawn on a\n57: 320-pixel-wide logical canvas at 1.25x, not upscaled from 256x192. The class\n58: \"crisp 2D\" in the O3DS tier is this atlas, not a software surface.\n59: \n60: ## 3D\n61: \n62: - The DS side interprets matrix stacks (20.12 fixed), texgen, and readable\n63:   box/position/vector tests on the CPU. NORMAL latches its transformed normal\n64:   and immutable lighting inputs; the PICA evaluates DS diffuse/specular,\n65:   shininess, ambient and emission with exact fixed-point rounding.\n66: - Vertices stay in object space. Each batch carries a palette of up to 16 clip\n67:   matrices; the 3DS side multiplies each by one fixup matrix (viewport,\n68:   widescreen x-scale, screen rotation, depth range) and the vertex shader\n69:   transforms on the GPU. Lit draws use six clip matrices to leave uniform\n70:   space for four lights and the shininess table; the vertex ABI stays 16 bytes.\n71: - The prior publish selects capture before the next scene starts, so field and\n72:   title producers can skip discarded geometry traversal and FIFO submission\n73:   while preserving game updates, animation and resource retirement.\n74: - Retained object-space meshes, the literal-colour baked block cache, and the\n75:   clip-volume side-plane cull are kohjoh's O3DS wins and are kept.\n76: - The box test is widened for widescreen so side content is not culled. That\n77:   widening is also the remaster's \"wider view\" for Platinum.\n78: \n79: Not implemented yet, and counted rather than silently dropped: fog, toon\n80: highlight, edge marking, shadow volumes, wireframe, display capture, bitmap\n81: BGs. The O3DS tier excludes sun shadows, edge marking, stereo, interpolation\n82: and xBRZ by design.\n83: \n84: ## Audio, content, storage\n85: \n86: - The vendored ARM7 sequencer and DS sound chip mix 32768 Hz stereo on an\n87:   audio thread (core 0, above the game), fed by NDSP. The decoded-ADPCM cache\n88:   is kohjoh's `adpcmClean` cache: voices whose decoder state comes from data\n89:   alone are decoded once.\n90: - The data pack is an indexed, versioned file keyed by original game file IDs.\n91:   The renderer, game and pack never know whether the pack is on SD or in RomFS.\n92: - Saves are two-generation raw payloads with a checked header, on SD for the\n93:   `.3dsx` and in the title archive for a `.cia`.\n94: \n95: ## Remaster feature map\n96: \n97: | Feature | Where it lives | O3DS cost |\n98: | --- | --- | --- |\n99: | Both screens filled | renderer viewports (2D 1.25x, 3D native 400x240) | flat |\n100: | Native-resolution 3D | g3d fixup + 400-wide targets | flat (GPU bound) |\n101: | Wider field view | g3d fixup x-scale + widened box test | few CPU tests |\n102: | Lower-screen menu | sinjoh game glue (`menu/`), not the renderer | 2D only |\n103: | Crisp 2D | g2d atlas | replaces software drawer |\n104: | WideArt | package-time bands loaded as textures | upload once |\n105: | Stable 30 Hz | pacing in `app/main.c`, present skip | measurement |\n106: | Pixel-perfect overworld | layout mode in the game glue | optional |\n107: \n108: Excluded on O3DS: 60 FPS interpolation, stereo, smooth3d 2x2, sun shadows,\n109: edge marking, xBRZ, full WideArt packs. The layout uses the reduced wide\n110: canvas; WideArt bands are precomputed, not synthesized per frame.\n111: \n112: ## What is deliberately different from pokeplatinum-3ds\n113: \n114: - No CPU transform/light/clip of 3D scenes, no software 2D rasterizer, no\n115:   GPU-to-CPU readback, no per-frame compositor upload.\n116: - No N3DS thread topology. The game owns the main thread; audio is the only\n117:   worker. Core 1 is treated as a shared system core, not a second full core.\n118: - No interpolation path to satisfy: the O3DS tier is 30 Hz by contract.\n119: - The patch stack is re-derived against the `kj_*` bridge instead of carrying\n120:   a second renderer's `NitroPort_*` API."

By itself the port fills those bands with rules (an edge colour\r\n5: going on, nothing; never a picture mirrored or stretched: see\r\n6: [REMASTER.md](REMASTER.md)).\r\n7: Where a rule doesn't look right, you can draw the bands yourself, screen by\r\n8: screen, and the game shows your drawing instead.\r\n9: \r\n10: ## How to\r\n11: \r\n12: 1. **Capture the screen.** The game on the 3DS has no button for it any\r\n13:    more (every button is the game's, since 2026-10-23): captures are made\r\n14:    with the PC runner (`pokeplatinum-pc`, [3ds_port/game/README.md](../3ds_port/game/README.md)),\r\n15:    run with `--wide --control DIR`: on the screen you want to draw, its\r\n16:    control command `capture WIDE` saves a capture into\r\n17:    `WIDE/captures/0001` (then `0002`, ...), WIDE being the wide folder\r\n18:    (`3ds/pokeplatinum/wide` on the SD card, or a copy). The captures\r\n19:    already made stay usable.\r\n20: 2. **Open WideArt.** It's `WideArt.exe` (no installing). The first time,\r\n21:    File > Open folder and pick the SD card, Azahar's `sdmc` folder, or\r\n22:    `3ds\\pokeplatinum\\wide`; it remembers. The captures are listed newest\r\n23:    first.\r\n24: 3. **Pick a layer and draw.** A screen is made of the game's layers: up to\r\n25:    four BGs and the sprites (OBJs), the sprites in groups (those of one\r\n26:    priority and palette: a scene's sprite background, like the strip\r\n27:    behind the Pokemon in the opening, is usually one group, \"Sprites,\r\n28:    palette 6\"). The list shows them front to back. Usually the one to draw\r\n29:    is the background, the backmost. The yellow lines are the DS's\r\n30:    picture's edges: the bands outside them are yours. To start, **Mirror**,\r\n31:    **Extend edge**, **Repeat** or **Clear** fills the bands from the\r\n32:    picture; then fix them by hand. The middle is locked so it can't be\r\n33:    changed by accident; untick \"Lock the DS's picture\" to change it too.\r\n34: 4. **Save** (Ctrl+S). The picture goes into `3ds/pokeplatinum/wide`, named\r\n35:    after the layer.\r\n36: 5. **Restart the game**: it reads the wide folder's pictures when it\r\n37:    starts. From then on, whenever that layer shows, your bands show with\r\n38:    it. (The PC runner reads them again with its control command\r\n39:    `wideart WIDE`.)\r\n40: \r\n41: ## The editor\r\n42: \r\n43: | | |\r\n44: |---|---|\r\n45: | Brush (B), Eraser (E) | round, 1 to 32 pixels across (the slider, or **[** and **]**); the eraser makes pixels transparent (the layers behind show). **Shift + click**: a straight line from where the last stroke ended |\r\n46: | Fill (G) | the area of one colour |\r\n47: | Pick colour (I), right-click | the colour under the cursor |\r\n48: | Select (M), Ctrl+A, Ctrl+D | drag a rectangle; then **drag inside it to cut and move those pixels** (hold Alt to move a copy, leaving them where they were). They float (an orange outline) until you put them down: Enter, a click outside, or another tool; Esc puts them back where they were. While floating: drag them again, the arrow keys move by 1 pixel (Shift: 8), H flips them, Delete throws them away |\r\n49: | Ctrl+T, R, Shift+R, H, Shift+H | scale and rotate the selection (by % and degrees, as you watch; 90° turns, flips; sharp pixels unless \"Smooth\"); turn it 90° right / left; flip it left-right / upside down. It stays floating, to drag into place |\r\n50: | Ctrl+X, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V | cut, copy, paste the selection; the paste floats where the copy came from (or in the selection), ready to drag into place. Ctrl+Shift+V pastes onto a new drawing layer |\r\n51: | Move (V) | drag the drawing layer (nothing selected), or the selection's pixels as Select does; the arrow keys move by 1 pixel, Shift+arrows by 8 |\r\n52: | Colour picker (click the colour) | a hue bar and a saturation/brightness square, the colour by H S B, R G B or hex; \"in the game\" is the colour as the DS shows it |\r\n53: | Recent, This screen's colours | the colours you used last; the colours the screen uses (drawing with them keeps the game's look) |\r\n54: | Ctrl+Z; Ctrl+Y or Ctrl+Shift+Z | undo; redo |\r\n55: | Alt + wheel (or Ctrl + wheel), +, - | zoom (1x to 12x), the pixel under the mouse staying under it |\r\n56: | Middle button drag (with or without Alt) | drag the whole picture round the window; Home puts it back in the middle |\r\n57: | P | the 3DS preview: the screen at the 3DS's size, as its filter shows it |\r\n58: | Layers in front: see-through | the layers in front of the one you're drawing, faint, so you can see it |\r\n59: | File > Open saved picture in another program | edit it in Aseprite, Photoshop...; then File > Reload saved picture |\r\n60: | File > Import picture (Ctrl+I), Export layer (Ctrl+Shift+E); the buttons under Save | to work on a picture in another program (Photoshop...) and bring it back: Export writes the layer as a PNG (320 x 192; a layout's picture at its own size), or (File) the drawing layer alone or the whole screen; Import puts a PNG or a PSD (Photoshop's, as one picture) in as a new drawing layer: a 320 x 192 one where it is, a layout's picture's own size at its place, anything else at the view's top-left, the Move tool chosen to drag it into place; Merge (Ctrl+E) puts it into the layer under it |\r\n61: \r\n62: **Drawing layers.** Each of the game's layers can have as many drawing\r\n63: layers of your own as you like, as in a paint program (the list under the\r\n64: game's layers, top first): **New** (Ctrl+Shift+N), **Duplicate** (Ctrl+J),\r\n65: **Delete**, **Show/Hide**, **Up**/**Down** (Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[), **Merge** down\r\n66: (Ctrl+E), **Rename** (F2, or double-click); Layer > Flatten all. Edit >\r\n67: Paste as a new layer (Ctrl+Shift+V) puts the copy on a layer of its own.\r\n68: Moving a drawing layer loses nothing that goes past the screen's edge: move\r\n69: it back and it's there. Saving puts the visible drawing layers together\r\n70: into the one picture the game reads, and keeps them as they are\r\n71: (`wide/editor/<key>_<hofs>_<vofs>/`) for next time. (If the saved picture\r\n72: was changed in another program since, the editor opens that instead.)\r\n73: \r\n74: **Scrolls round all the time (a strip).** Tick it for a layer that keeps\r\n75: scrolling (the opening's blue strip): its bands then move with it all the\r\n76: time. Otherwise a layer's bands show only while it's where you drew it\r\n77: (see below).\r\n78: \r\n79: **A screen's own pictures.** The pictures a screen's layout draws itself\r\n80: (the party's panel, its Poké Ball and lights, the boxes' divider: see\r\n81: \"Pictures a screen's layout draws\" below) are in its captures too, as\r\n82: layers \"Picture: <name>\", each just in front of the BG it's drawn with,\r\n83: unturned (a ball captured mid-turn shows upright). Draw on them like any\r\n84: layer (nothing is locked for them), move them anywhere (the Move tool) and\r\n85: save: the editor writes the file (`wide/<name>.png`) as the box round\r\n86: what's drawn, wherever it is, what's past the screen's edge too (the\r\n87: party's ball, half off the screen). Moved from the layout's place, the\r\n88: file also says how far (its PNG `oFFs` chunk): the game draws it there,\r\n89: and turns it about the middle of what's drawn. (A picture saved straight\r\n90: from another program loses that and goes back to its place: bring it in\r\n91: with File > Import instead.) A light's colours are a picture each: a\r\n92: capture has the ones that were lit then.\r\n93: \r\n94: **Screens laid out in parts.** On the screens the port lays out anew (the\r\n95: party, the boxes, the bag, the summary...: see \"Pictures a screen's\r\n96: layout draws\" below), the game moves the layers itself. A picture of one\r\n97: of those layers made right where it is in a capture (drawn on: the boxes'\r\n98: panel's edges cleaned) is used as it is: the whole layer, or its bands\r\n99: with the game's layout between. Captured where the layer is somewhere\r\n100: else (a box's wallpaper mid-slide), the game's own layout shows.\r\n101: \r\n102: Colours are saved as the DS shows them (5 bits a channel), and pixels are\r\n103: either solid or transparent (no half-transparent ones).\r\n104: \r\n105: The editor's own preview puts the layers on top of each other without the\r\n106: game's blending effects (some screens blend two layers, the title screen\r\n107: for one), nor the 3D (a capture doesn't have it); the game shows the real\r\n108: thing.\r\n109: \r\n110: ## What the game does with it\r\n111: \r\n112: A picture belongs to a layer by its **key**: a fingerprint of that layer's\r\n113: art (a BG's map, the tiles it uses, their colours; a sprite group's\r\n114: tiles and colours, not how many sprites show them or how they're cut), not of where the game put it in memory or how\r\n115: it's scrolled. The slide is made as wide as the\r\n128:     screen: in the last 32 pixels before something is whole on the DS's\r\n129:     screen it moves twice as far, so it comes in from the wide screen's\r\n130:     edge, and what waits beyond the DS's edge to come in waits beyond the\r\n131:     wide screen's too (no Pokemon's hand showing before it comes in).\r\n132:     Past the picture's own edges the layer's map goes on. If the layer\r\n133:     has a picture made further along, the one whose own edge wouldn't come\r\n134:     into view is used (the opening's Torterra, cut by the wide screen's\r\n135:     edge in both of his);\r\n136:   - **scrolls round all the time** (`_loop`, the editor's \"Scrolls round\r\n137:     all the time\"): its bands move with it everywhere, and past the\r\n138:     picture's edge they go round as the layer's map does (the opening's\r\n139:     blue strip); where a picture of the bands only has moved so far that\r\n140:     its middle comes in beside the DS's screen, the layer's own pixels\r\n141:     show there (they're what the middle was);\r\n142: - one layer can have **several pictures**, one for each place it was\r\n143:   captured at: the opening's sky and its blue strip are the same layer (one\r\n144:   tall map, the sky above, the strip below), each with its own picture.\r\n145:   The game uses the one made nearest where the layer is, if that's less\r\n146:   than a screen away; capturing the layer a few pixels from a picture's\r\n147:   place opens that picture, lined up, and saving it replaces it;\r\n148: - if the layer's own art changes (text printed into it, a palette fading,\r\n149:   a sprite animating), the key changes and the port's own rules come back\r\n150:   until it's the same art again. Text boxes and menus are usually on layers\r\n151:   of their own, so the background layer keeps its key.\r\n152: \r\n153: A sprite group's picture goes where the group has no sprite, at the\r\n154: group's priority (so the layers in front of the sprites stay in front).\r\n155: It adds to the sprites, it can't take any of their pixels away: a sprite\r\n156: drawn over or rubbed out in the editor still shows (the shop's cursor's\r\n157: right end, in a picture that widened it). Where a picture reaches the DS's edge, draw the layer as it\r\n164: should be: move it (Move tool) so that what the DS cut at its edge is cut\r\n165: at the wide screen's edge, and draw the strips on to the edges. (Without CAPTURE: all\r\n179: the captures; without `--write` it only lists them.) Every polygon edge is smooth, the outlines one pixel\n262: wide as before (their outer side softened by the smooth pixels next to\n263: them). `smooth3d stereo` keeps the smooth 3D to the slider up. A frame\n264: with the slider up and outlines took about 2 x 12.5 ms of the GPU's by\n265: the measures so far (2026-10-20): the frames in flight (Timing) are what\n266: let it keep 30 frames a second.\n267: \n268: The 3D's textures are RGBA5551 where that's exact (every DS format but\n269: A3I5 and A5I3, sampled nearest, as `filter3d 0` has it: the DS's colours\n270: are 5 bits a channel, those formats' texels opaque or not there), RGBA8\n271: otherwise. A frame draws the opaque\n272: polygons nine times with outlines on, those with see-through texels\n273: textured each time: in tall grass and among trees the GPU took 22-30 ms a\n274: frame of the 33 (2026-10-15), and RGBA8 textures were twice the memory to\n275: read.\n276: \n277: Fog: the DS fogs a pixel by its depth, through a 32-entry density table\n278: starting at FOG_OFFSET, each entry 0x400 >> FOG_SHIFT depth units on\n279: (DISP3DCNT). The PICA's fog takes a 128-entry table over its own depth, so\n280: each scene's depth is put back into the DS's units (the vertex depth is\n281: the DS's z or w, normalised per scene, linear) and the table is worked out\n282: from the DS's (`setup_fog`, `fog_density`). Polygons fog where their\n283: attribute's fog bit is set; the rear plane where the clear colour's is.\n284: The intro's forest uses it (white fog, a linear table). The table goes\n285: to the GPU once per scene's draw (citro3d sends all 128 entries whenever\n286: it's bound; it was bound for each batch).\n287: \n288: The field at the DS's pixel size sees 24 lines more above the DS's top\n289: row, further away than the DS ever shows, and the fog (made for the DS's\n290: view) went on thickening there: the mountains and buildings at the top of\n291: the screen washed out to the fog's colour, as if cut off (Route 206's\n292: Cycling Road, 2026-11-01). With a view taller than the DS's, the fog is\n293: held at the DS's top row's: the farthest depth within its 192 rows (the\n294: scene's vertices there, and where their triangles' edges cross the rows'\n295: top and bottom: `ds_rows_farthest`), the table's entries beyond it as at\n296: it, the rear plane no thicker. Logged now and then: `[compose] the taller\n297: view's fog held at the DS's top row's`.\n298: \n299: A scene is drawn with the 3D registers the game had at its SWAP_BUFFERS\n300: (DISP3DCNT and 0x320-0x3BF: the clear colour, the fog, the outlines'\n301: colours; noted on the game's thread with the swap:\n302: `NitroGx3dScene.disp3dcnt`, `regs3d`), not as they are when it's drawn, a\n303: few V-blanks later.\n304: \n305: The vertex program (`gx3d_passthrough.v.pica`) does the view (where the\n306: DS's screen goes on the 3DS's turned framebuffer) and the stereoscopic\n307: shift: `x += strength * max(w - convergence, -w)`, for perspective\n308: vertices (w > 1) only. The convergence (the depth that's at the screen)\n309: is the middle of where most of a scene's perspective vertices are: the\n310: geometric mean of the 5th and the 95th percentile of their w, so a few\n311: polygons near the camera or far away don't move it; and the eyes follow\n312: it a tenth of the way (in octaves) each new scene, not at once, and not\n313: again for the in-between scenes. Taken from the nearest and the farthest\n314: vertex, each scene, it jumped when something came on screen, and every\n315: polygon's shift with it: the geometry flickered with the slider up.\n316: \n317: The GPU's command list is 1 MB; a draw that wouldn't fit is left out\n318: rather than overflow it (an overflow stopped the GPU thread on the real\n319: 3DS). The `[perf] display` line says how full it got.\n320: \n321: Publishing a 2D picture (the drawing threads): the 15-bit pixels to\n322: RGB565, each doubled into the tiled texture (a 4x4 block of pixels is one\n323: 8x8 tile), and the layers in front to RGBA8 with the alpha multiplied in.\n324: With the sharp filter (the default) only what changed is done again\n325: (`NitroPort_PublishDoubled`): each engine's last picture is kept, and each\n326: band of 4 rows (a row of the texture's tiles) remembers the publish it\n327: last changed in; a set of textures gets the bands changed since it was\n328: last written, and only those are flushed. Most changes are small (a\n329: location's name sliding in, a text box, a cursor): done whole, engine A's\n330: picture took ~10 ms a frame on the core the 3D's geometry shares, and\n331: frames came late while a name slid in. The other filters publish the\n332: whole picture, the layers in front only when there's anything there.\n333: \n334: What counts as a change of the picture (the drawers draw again only\n335: then) leaves out DISP3DCNT's two acknowledge bits: the game writes them\n336: every frame, alternating, and the field's upper screen was drawn and\n337: published again every other frame with nothing on it changed.\n338: \n339: What's approximate, compared with the DS's compositing: a 2D layer in\n340: front of the 3D blends with the 3D by its alpha (eva / 16) where the DS\n341: blends by eva and evb separately; a 3D first target of alpha blending\n342: (BLDCNT bit 0 with the alpha effect) isn't blended with the layer behind;\n343: a brightness effect on the 3D applies to the whole 3D area regardless of\n344: windows; the fog's alpha-only mode isn't drawn. `tests/test_render.c`\n345: (`test_split_layers`, `test_wide_canvas`) checks the two layers put\n346: together give the same picture as the renderer draws in one, where the\n347: DS's result is exactly reproducible, and that the wider canvas's middle is\n348: the DS's picture.\n349: \n350: ### H-blank effects: the screen changed line by line\n351: \n352: Some of the game's effects change the display's registers while the DS\n353: draws the screen, between lines (an H-blank interrupt handler, or a DMA\n354: that writes a register at every line): the start of a battle slices the\n355: screen into bands that slide apart (the grass), splits it (a trainer),\n356: waves it (water, caves); some moves wave the battle's background. The\n357: port draws a whole frame at once, so it goes through the frame's lines\n358: first (`NitroPort_HBlankLinesOnce`, port_os.c, on the game's thread before\n359: the display state is taken; once a V-blank: the game arms its H-blank\n360: DMAs again only in its V-blank interrupt): before each line it runs that\n361: H-blank's DMAs and interrupt handler, with the V-count the game reads for\n362: it and DISPSTAT's H-blank flag set (some handlers check it), and keeps\n363: each line's registers (`NitroPort_LineRegs`: each engine's first 0x70\n364: bytes, but DISPSTAT and the V-count). The 2D renderer draws each line with\n365: its own BG scroll, windows and affine matrices, and gives the compositor\n366: the 3D's scroll on each line (`scroll3dLine`). The compositor draws the\n367: 3D a run of lines at a time, each run moved by its scroll and drawn\n368: inside its rows alone (the viewport of its rows, the view moved to match,\n369: so the GPU clips the polygons to the run: `PicaView.band`; and the\n370: scissor, set again by each of the scene's passes: `PicaView.scissor`; the\n371: scissor alone still had every run's polygons gone through everywhere, 62\n372: ms of the GPU a frame at a battle's start), its rear plane and its\n373: brightness tint too:\n374: at most 24 runs (12 an eye with the slider up), and no more than the GPU's\n375: command list has room for (each run is the scene's commands again); more\n376: lines are put together by an odd number of runs (lines sliding apart by\n377: turns stay apart by turns). Frames with runs aren't counted by the 60\n378: frames a second steps. Each run draws only the scene's triangles that can\n379: reach its rows (`NitroPort_Gx3dTriangleRows`, once a scene: each\n380: triangle's rows as -y / w of its corners; `NitroPort_Gx3dBandRanges`:\n381: each batch's parts with them, the run 2 rows more each side; a corner not\n382: in front of the camera, every run): the GPU clipped the others away, but\n383: went through all of them in every run, the whole scene's vertices and\n384: state 24 times a frame. The grass's slices took the GPU 17.1 ms a frame\n385: and the display thread 14.3 ms building it (a log of 2026-11-04: 40\n386: frames a second at the wild Pokémon's battle start, less with the slider\n387: up); on the PC's scenes of it each run now has about a tenth of the\n388: triangles and a quarter of the batches. `test_band_ranges`: a run's\n389: pixels (depth and polygon ID, drawn as the GPU puts them) the same as\n390: with every triangle, the slider up or down, the 3D moved past the edge.\n391: That still left each run about 0.3 ms of the GPU beyond its pixels (the\n392: next log: 15.1 ms a frame, the slices moving 15 to 30 times a second, 10\n393: or 18 lines high instead of 2). So where it can, the compositor draws the\n394: 3D once an eye into a texture of its own (`draw_slices`: 256 x 512, the\n395: screen's 240 x 400 at its corner, the GPU's framebuffer there too, the\n396: viewport only those: `PicaView.viewWidth`), unscrolled, as the screen\n397: would have it (its rear plane, its polygons), then every one of the DS's\n398: runs from it at its own scroll, a textured quad each, in one draw, and\n399: the 3D's tint over the same quads: the grass's 96 slices of 2 lines\n400: exactly (each moved by whole pixels, so every pixel takes one texel's\n401: middle). What's behind the 3D: with a rear plane that hides it, or all\n402: one colour (the texture filled with it), the texture is all there is;\n403: else, the texture RGBA8 (filled with alpha 0) and no rear plane (the\n404: field's: its clear colour's alpha is 0), the 3D's empty pixels are left\n405: out of the quads (the alpha test) and the screen's own picture shows\n406: there. Only on the upper screen, the 3D inside it, no outlines; else the\n407: runs as above. The first log (2026-11-04) had a battle's start with\n408: what's behind the 3D not one colour: the stretched picture's (the log\n409: now says where, once: `[compose] a battle's start: behind the 3D`). It's taken even where the command list had room\n410: for only one run (that run would have drawn the effect unsliced). With\n411: the slider up the right eye goes the left eye's way. The\n412: log says the way each time it changes (`[compose] an H-blank effect's 3D\n413: (96 runs of lines) drawn from its texture`, or why not), 24 times at\n414: most. The 3D is at the screen's own pixels then (the\n415: 2x2 smooth 3D's texels doubled) for the moment of the effect. The texture\n416: is made the first time it's needed, when VRAM has room for it (RGBA8, 1\n417: MB with its depth/stencil; else RGB565, 768 KB, only for the first two\n418: cases) and 512 KB more (the outlines' copies come later), its quads in linear\n419: memory of their own (126 KB); the log says which (`[compose] an H-blank\n420: effect's 3D drawn once into a texture`, or `no room for the H-blank\n421: effects' texture`: the runs as above).\n422: The game moves the slices 30 times a second (once a game step). At 60\n423: frames a second they move each frame, halfway in the in-between frames, as\n424: the 3D's camera does; their black edges go with them. Those edges are the\n425: game's windows (window 0 the part a slice moved one way shows, window 1 the\n426: part of one moved the other way it hides), so they're left out of the\n427: picture for the compositor to draw (`NitroRender2DSplit.gpuSpans`): on a\n428: battle's start stretched over the screen, with the 3D's lines scrolled\n429: apart, where every line's windows show everything (the colour effects too)\n430: or nothing, in one part at most, no OBJ window or circle, something is\n431: hidden, and nothing is in front of the 3D (a trainer's battle start slides\n432: two halves with the halves of a Poké Ball, sprites the picture draws: the\n433: windows stay in the picture then, all of it at 30 as before) (`gpuSpansOn`,\n434: each line's shown part `spanLo` to `spanHi`). The\n435: picture's `over` then shows nothing where the windows hide the 3D, rather\n436: than what's behind it, and the compositor draws the backdrop there after\n437: the layers in front (`draw_window_edges`), on the lines the 3D was drawn\n438: with. The game's thread notes each frame's lines (each line's 3D scroll and\n439: shown part, `NitroPort_Render2DLineSpansNow`, while a battle's start plays:\n440: `NitroPort_ComposeNoteLines`), found by the scene's frame as the BGs'\n441: scrolls are; the slices from the texture and their edges are those of the\n442: frame shown, and in an in-between frame halfway from the frame before's\n443: (`NitroPort_LineSpansHalfway`: each line's scroll the shorter way round,\n444: its scroll finer than a pixel, more than 128 pixels after's; a part's\n445: edges halfway, a part shrinking away to nothing going towards the side it\n446: touched; a side hidden in one frame only no further than the line's 3D,\n447: moved halfway, leaves uncovered: the grass's slices change sides as they\n448: start going apart, from 3 pixels one way to 29 the other, and the 4\n449: columns hidden on the left before would have covered 2 of the 3D moved 13\n450: the other way). A new scene without an in-between one gets an in-between\n451: frame of its own when the slices moved (`lines_moved`: slices in both\n452: frames, as the sprites). The lines are noted only while the upper\n453: screen's picture is a battle's start stretched.\n454: Drawn a run at a time (no texture, the outlines), the slices and their\n455: edges are the picture's, as before. The PC runner's `pshot` draws the\n456: edges as the 3DS does, the same pictures as with them in `over`;\n457: `test_gpu_spans` has the grass's lines as the game sets them.\n458: The colour effects and OAM are the frame's (no\n459: effect of the game's changes those by line). Without an H-blank interrupt\n460: or DMA nothing of this runs; in the field the game keeps its H-blank\n461: interrupt on, so its handler runs 193 times a frame there (with nothing to\n462: do: the lines don't differ, and nothing is drawn differently). Without the\n463: remaster (the drawers read the game's live state) the lines are gone\n464: through only while no drawer reads them.\n465: \n466: Before this (2026-10-21) the effects showed as the frame's last line had\n467: the registers: the whole screen jumped, then went black.\n468: \n469: Not yet: display capture (the legendary Pokémon's motion blur at the\n470: start of their battles), the main-memory display mode.\n471: \n472: ## The wider screen\n473: \n474: The upper screen's 2D is drawn on a canvas 320 DS pixels wide, the DS's\n475: x = 0 at 32 (`NitroRender2DSplit.width`/`origin`, laid out by\n476: `NitroPort_WideLayout` in `port_wide.c`). The rules, so that nothing is\n477: stretched:\n478: \n479: - **Hand-drawn bands win.** A layer (a BG, or a group of sprites) with a\n480:   picture drawn for it shows that picture in its bands (or all over): see\n481:   [WIDE_ART.md](WIDE_ART.md).\n482: - **The DS's layout stays, but for the edges.** The game's windows,\n483:   menus and sprites keep their places, but for the windows that go to the\n484:   screen's edges (below), which take their sprites with them (moved apart,\n485:   a menu's icons and its window came apart). Nothing is stretched.\n486: - **A plain edge goes on.** Where a BG's line is one colour at its edge (a\n487:   picture's plain border, the black of a fade, a window's frame) that\n488:   colour goes on to the screen's edge: for 8 pixels at the edge, or on the\n489:   screens made of pictures (`NitroPort_WidePictures`) for 32, a band's\n490:   width, so that nothing of a picture is drawn out (the opening strip's\n491:   ovals were, into lines).\n492: - **Nothing is mirrored.** A picture that reaches the DS's edge (the\n493:   intro's scenery, the title's torn border) isn't folded over into the\n494:   bands any more: those screens have pictures drawn for them (see\n495:   [WIDE_ART.md](WIDE_ART.md)); without one, its bands stay empty.\n496: - **The UI's backgrounds go on beside the DS's screen.** Where a line of\n497:   a BG has something at the DS's edge that isn't plain (a menu's panel\n498:   reaching it), the plain lines next to it are carried on through it, in\n499:   their pattern (every 1 to 8 lines: the party list's stripes go on\n500:   behind its panels). Where a BG has nothing at the edge, nothing goes\n501:   beside it (the backdrop, or the 3D). (Before October 2026, nothing went\n502:   beside a line that wasn't plain, and the party list, the summary and\n503:   the bag had black blocks in the bands.)\n504: - **Pictures with plain middles and decorated sides** (the intro's red\n505:   bars) are split: each half goes to its screen edge and the plain middle\n506:   widens.\n507: - **The DS's windows** (its hardware windows, WIN0/1) at the DS's edges go\n508:   on to the screen's: the intro's letterbox covers the bands too. A window\n509:   from 0 to 255 counts as reaching the right edge (the register can't say\n510:   256, so it leaves the DS's last column out; the bands went black beside\n511:   the intro's city). An empty window (0 to 0: the circle wipes' lines\n512:   past their circle) covers nothing, the bands included (the Town Map's\n513:   side bars showed in them while its circle closed). Where a circle is\n514:   wider than the DS's screen, the game's window stops at its edges, so\n515:   for those few lines the bands are inside it.\n516: - **The battle background** is a 512-pixel map (the trainer's slide-in\n517:   scrolls across it): the picture, then the same picture mirrored. After\n518:   the intro the game draws the platforms (the terrain's sprites) into it\n519:   (`BattleSystem_BakeSpritesToBackground`), and puts the player's\n520:   platform's left part just left of the picture, where the map goes on\n521:   past the DS's left edge. Beside the DS's screen the map's own pixels show\n522:   where it has a picture of its own (that platform part, the same for\n523:   every terrain), and where it only has the mirror, the map's pixel next\n524:   to the DS's edge goes on: the background's own edge, from before the\n525:   platforms (the DS's edge pixel is a platform's where one reaches the\n526:   edge: the Elite Four's, on the right). Until 2026-10-16 the bands\n527:   repeated the DS's edge pixel, and the player's platform was drawn out\n528:   into lines.\n529: - **The place name sign** goes to the screen's left edge while it shows:\n530:   the game tells the port (`patches/pokeplatinum/0014`,\n531:   `NitroPort_WindowAnchor`; patch 0012 tells it where the windows are).\n532: - **Menus by the DS's edge go to the screen's edge.** The game tells the\n533:   port which windows have a frame drawn round them (patch 0015,\n534:   `NitroPort_WindowFramed`): a menu's (a tile all round) or a text box's\n535:   (2 tiles left, 3 right). A framed window within 2 tiles of the DS's left\n536:   or right edge goes to the wider screen's edge, as far from it as it was\n537:   from the DS's (the field menu, YES/NO, the save's summary, a shop's\n538:   list, the party's menus); one in the middle, or across the screen,\n539:   stays. The sprites over a moved window go with it (the field menu's\n540:   icons).\n541: - **The battle's text box** has its frame's edges clear and the ground\n542:   under it (patch 0040, 2026-10-25): the game fills a frame's clear pixels\n543:   with its colour 10 in battles (black in 19 of the 20 frames), and the\n544:   battle's background has nothing under the box (rows 20-23), so a black\n545:   box showed behind it, wider for the wider box. Now the clear pixels stay\n546:   clear and the background's last row of pictures (the ground, row 19) is\n547:   carried on down through rows 20-23.\n548: - **Text boxes span the screen.** A text box across the DS's screen has\n549:   its frame's left part at the screen's left edge and its right part at\n550:   the right edge, each line of the frame's inner columns drawn on between\n551:   them; the text starts a pixel inside the frame's left part (2026-10-16,\n552:   from a drawing of the PC's text box: the room the wider screen gives is\n553:   used, the text at the left as on the DS). Its lines stay as the game\n554:   broke them. What's drawn on right of the text is the window's own last\n555:   column (its top and bottom borders and the box's inside), whatever the\n556:   frame (2026-10-25): it was the frame's right part's first column, which\n557:   in many of the 20 frames is the frame's own drawing, a red or dark band\n558:   across the box (the battle's text box after the frame was changed).\n559:   On a line of text that reaches that last column it's the inside's plain\n560:   colour instead, from the nearest column left of the letters that has it\n561:   (the colour of the nearest line above or below with nothing on it in\n562:   the window's last 24 columns, 16 lines at most: `WidenLinePlain`):\n563:   Camper Jacob's \"Hey, how about you and me battle before\" on Route 205\n564:   ends in the last column, and its e was drawn on to the box's right as a\n565:   grey line (2026-11-06). On the PC that box now has nothing past the e.\n566:   In `test_render.c`: `test_wide_framed_windows` (a letter's column there,\n567:   and a line red all along the last 24 columns: white drawn on).\n568: - **Screens redrawn for the wider screen.** For a screen with a reference\n569:   drawn for the wider screen, the game lays the screen out in parts that\n570:   move apart (`NitroPort_WideSplitScreen`): on given lines of given BGs,\n571:   what's left of a column moves one way and what's right of it the other,\n572:   with that column drawn on between them (a card's body, widened) or\n573:   nothing (the text over it). Only the DS's 256 columns move, nothing from\n574:   beyond them. On an affine BG the parts are laid out on the BG's own\n575:   picture, before its matrix, so a card that turns over keeps its layout\n576:   as it turns; its hand-drawn picture, if there is one, goes through the\n577:   matrix too. The trainer card (patch 0016, 2026-10-15): its body is 31\n578:   pixels wider each side; the fields and their values sit at its left\n579:   edge and the photo at its right; TIME, ADVENTURE STARTED and the back's\n580:   rows have their labels at the left and their values at the right; the\n581:   signature stays in the middle of its widened box.\n582: - **Screens laid out in parts** (`NitroPort_WideScreenParts`, patches\n583:   0017-0022, 2026-10-16). The splits are a case of these. An app gives\n584:   the port its screen as a list of parts, when the screen changes, and\n585:   none when it ends (`include/port_wide_layout.h` in the decompilation):\n586:   a BG's columns moved (MOVE), a BG's column drawn on where others would\n587:   be (FILL), the sprites in a rectangle moved (OBJS; stretched: their edge\n588:   column drawn back to where they were, a cursor as wide as its row), the\n589:   3D moved (SHIFT3D). On a BG's line with parts, the DS's picture shows\n590:   where it is but for the columns MOVEs take, and each part is drawn over\n591:   it in turn (a column shows the last part over it); beside the DS's\n592:   screen, only what parts put there. Lines and columns are the BG's\n593:   picture's (they go with its scroll), or the DS's screen's (a box's\n594:   wallpapers sliding past behind a fixed edge). A moved BG shows its own\n595:   pixels, not a hand-drawn picture of it, and moved sprites themselves;\n596:   a screen's static backgrounds keep their pictures (the Pokédex's pages).\n597:   But a text BG's picture made right where it is (a capture of the screen\n598:   as its parts lay it out, drawn on in the editor: the boxes' panel's\n599:   edges, cleaned, 2026-10-16) is that layer: all of it (a whole-layer\n600:   picture), or its bands with the parts between.\n601:   From references drawn for the wider screen:\n602:   - the summary: the left column (name, picture, item) toward the left\n603:     edge, each page's panel widened to the right edge with its values\n604:     there, the move details, the memo and contest pages, the exit page;\n605:   - the party: the panels 32 to the right, the background widened left;\n606:   - the bag: the bag and its pockets left, the list widened to the right\n607:     edge (counts at the edge, the cursor as wide as its row), the\n608:     description box widened across, its text by the item's icon;\n609:   - the boxes: the panel of the Pokémon looked at at the left edge, the\n610:     box at the right edge (its party tray, icons, hand and buttons with\n611:     it), the wallpaper's edge between; the boxes to jump to and an item's\n612:     description across the middle; the message box widened like a text\n613:     box, the menus at the right edge;\n614:   - the Pokédex's list: its label and picture left, its rows and scroll\n615:     bar right, the counts apart.\n616:   - the Pokédex's page after a catch (patch 0040, 2026-10-25), in the\n617:     battle: its maps are 256 wide, so they came round beside the DS's\n618:     screen (the entry's picture frame and text box over again). Now as the\n619:     info page's picture has it: the banner on to the edges, the\n620:     background's pattern beside the DS's screen, the text box's ends at the\n621:     screen's edges and its middle drawn on between.\n622:   - the Pokédex's cry page (patch 0040, 2026-10-25): the wave from edge to\n623:     edge. The DS draws it a few columns a frame into a 256-wide map it\n624:     scrolls, the oldest columns coming round next to the newest at its\n625:     right (a glitch at the wave's end); here it's drawn into a 512-wide\n626:     window of its own, the newest columns at the wider screen's right edge,\n627:     the map shown on beside the DS's screen (SHOW parts, below); the rest\n628:     of that map is a clear tile. Its band's lower edge is 3 lines lower, at\n629:     the screen's bottom (the DS has 3 lines of the page's background under\n630:     it, which looked like a mistake there), drawn on the wave's layer (shown\n631:     beside the DS's screen and faded with the page), so the background\n632:     layer's hand-drawn picture still fits it.\n633:   - the shop's list (patch 0026, 2026-10-17): its box 31 pixels wider\n634:     to the right, the prices at its right edge, the cursor as wide as its\n635:     row, the scroll arrows at its middle; the green panel below across the\n636:     screen (the money's and the quantity's windows go by the screen's\n637:     edges, as windows do). The bands are physical 0..40 and 360..400 (32 logical px each).\n- I need to draw band content in those regions, per layer, in DS priority order.\n\nImplementation sketch (engine):\n- In `draw_span`, when the screen is the top screen (wide), for each BG layer drawn, also draw its \"band\" quads: a quad covering the left band (logical x -32..0) and the right band (logical 256..288) with the band's content.\n- The band's content: either a wideart picture (precomputed texture) or the edge-color extension.\n\nFor the edge-color extension, we need per-row colors at the layer's edge. That requires reading the layer's rendered pixels at the edge — which the atlas doesn't have (it's tile-based). Alternative: compute the edge color per row from the BG's map/tiles — complex (affine, scrolling).\n\nAlternative approach that is much simpler and GPU-native: **render the layer's band by drawing the layer's tiles again, but with a modified transform** that shifts the layer horizontally by ±256 (or by the map's wrap) so the layer's own art continues into the band. That's the \"the map goes on past the DS's edge\" idea. For a text BG with a 256-wide map, there's no more map. For a 512-wide map, there is.\n\nHmm, p3ds's rules: \"Nothing is mirrored. A picture that reaches the DS's edge isn't folded over into the bands any more: those screens have pictures drawn for them; without one, its bands stay empty.\" and \"A plain edge goes on. Where a BG's line is one colour at its edge... that colour goes on to the screen's edge\".\n\nSo p3ds does NOT continue the map; it extends plain edge colors, and for non-plain edges it leaves the bands empty (black) or uses wideart.\n\nSo implementing \"edge color extension\" requires knowing the rendered edge pixels per row. In sinjoh's atlas renderer, we could compute this from the tile data: for each row y in the layer, look at the tile column at x=0 (and x=255) and check if the 8 pixels are the same color index → then get the palette color. Doable for text BGs (non-affine, no scroll offset complications, though scroll shifts which column is at the edge).\n\nCost: for each of 192 rows, look up 2 tiles' pixel rows (8 pixels each) and compare indices → 192*16 = 3072 byte lookups + palette lookups. That's fine per layer change, but the scroll changes every frame in the field (so the edge column changes). Hmm, but the scroll is a register change; the retained layer cache rebuilds when registers change... so every frame in the field. 3072 lookups/frame is maybe 20-30 µs. Acceptable-ish on O3DS but adds up.\n\nSimplification: only compute the band when the layer covers the screen edge *and* the edge is plain. We could compute it lazily per row and cache per (layer, scroll).\n\nHmm. This is getting deep. Let me consider the *pragmatic* order of work:\n\nThe most visible remaster element, and the one the user explicitly named, is **wideart precomputed at package time**.       "text": "Instructions from: C:\\Users\\terezi\\workdir\\sinjoh\\AGENTS.md\n# AGENTS.md\r\n\r\nRepository-wide rules for agent sessions working on kohjoh.\r\n\r\n## READ THE WIKI \r\n\r\nYou're not expected to have deep technical knowledge of the 3DS platform or how to program efficiently for it. This is not optional, and it matters most for implementer agents: they edit files and cannot rely on chat context the lead has not written down.\r\n\r\nEvery subagent brief must state, in the prompt itself:\r\n\r\n1. **Objective** — the one bounded slice to complete, and why it exists.\r\n2. **Allowed paths** — the exact files or directories the subagent may read and edit.\r\n3. **Deliverables** — the concrete output: code, patch files, tests, docs, and the required report format (files changed, commands run, results, open questions).\r\n4. **Acceptance checks** — the commands or observations that prove the work is done, and the expected result.\r\n5. **Avoidables** — what not to touch or do: paths outside the slice, unrelated refactors, the decomp checkout in place, commits/pushes unless explicitly assigned, and any known traps from `kohjoh.md` or `docs/troubleshooting.md`.\r\n6. **Stopping point** — when to stop and report instead of guessing, for example if the slice grows, the brief conflicts with `kohjoh.md`, or an acceptance check cannot pass.\r\n\r\nDo not send a subagent a vague goal and let it infer scope. If the lead cannot fill in all six items, the slice is not ready to delegate. A brief that is broader, vaguer or in conflict with `kohjoh.md` should be revised before the call, not discovered by the subagent mid-edit.\r\n\r\nImplementer subagents hold `docs/status.md`, `docs/lessons.md` and `kohjoh.md` as required reading; the brief adds the slice-specific detail those files cannot contain.               "newString": "    return h != 0 ? h : 1;\n}\n\n/* ---------------------------------------------------------- the wide art */\n\n/*\n * The wide art: the hand-drawn bands beside the DS's picture (wideart.h).\n *\n * The remaster's upper screen is 32 DS pixels wider on each side than the\n * DS's picture, and the game draws nothing there. What the game draws past the DS's\n * edge (a map going on) is not drawn into the band: that is the port's own\n * rule's work (docs/PORTING.md, the wide screen), and it is not done yet.\n *\n * The wide canvas: 320 DS pixels, the DS's picture at x 32..287, the bands\n * at 0..31 and 288..319.\n */\n\n#define WIDE_CANVAS_W 320\n#define WIDE_BAND_W 32\n#define WIDE_ORIGIN 32 /* the DS's picture starts here */\n\n/* How far the layer may have scrolled from where the picture was made and\n * still show its bands (pokeplatinum-3ds's ART_REST). */\n#define ART_REST 8\n\n/* One band: a rectangle of the picture's texture, at the canvas's x. */\nstatic void put_band_quad(kj_v2d *v, int x, int y, int w, int h, int tx, int ty)\n{\n    const int16_t u0 = (int16_t)(tx * KJ_UV_UNIT + 1);\n    const int16_t u1 = (int16_t)((tx + w) * KJ_UV_UNIT - 1);\n    const int16_t v0 = (int16_t)(ty * KJ_UV_UNIT + 1);\n    const int16_t v1 = (int16_t)((ty + h) * KJ_UV_UNIT - 1);\n    v[0] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)x, (int16_t)y, u0, v0, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n    v[1] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)(x + w), (int16_t)y, u1, v0, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n    v[2] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)x, (int16_t)(y + h), u0, v1, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n    v[3] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)(x + w), (int16_t)(y + h), u1, v1, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n}\n\n/*\n * The bands of a layer's picture, as quads. What is left of the canvas's band is the picture's\n * middle: the game's own, which the layer draws itself.\n */\nstatic void band_quads(const kj_wideart_pic *pic, int dx, drawable *out)\n{\n    uint32_t first;\n    kj_v2d *v;\n\n    out->base = NULL;\n    out->count = 0;\n    v = kj_gpu_quads_alloc(2, &first);\n    if (v == NULL) {\n        return;\n    }\n    const int bh = pic->band_h;\n    uint32_t n = 0;\n\n    /* the left band: the picture's x 0..31 */\n    int lo = dx > 0 ? 0 : -dx;\n    int hi = dx > 0 ? WIDE_BAND_W - dx : WIDE_BAND_W;\n    if (hi > WIDE_BAND_W) {\n        hi = WIDE_BAND_W;\n    }\n    if (hi > lo) {\n        put_band_quad(v + n * 4u, lo - WIDE_ORIGIN, 0, hi - lo, bh, pic->left_x + (lo + dx), pic->left_y);\n        ++n;\n    }\n\n    /* the right band: the picture's x 288..319 */\n    const int rx0 = WIDE_CANVAS_W - WIDE_BAND_W;\n    lo = dx > 0 ? rx0 : rx0 - dx;\n    hi = dx > 0 ? WIDE_CANVAS_W - dx : WIDE_CANVAS_W;\n    if (hi > WIDE_CANVAS_W) {\n        hi = WIDE_CANVAS_W;\n    }\n    if (hi > lo) {\n        put_band_quad(v + n * 4u, lo - WIDE_ORIGIN, 0, hi - lo, bh, pic->right_x + (lo + dx - rx0),\n                      pic->right_y);\n        ++n;\n    }\n\n    out->first = first;\n    out->count = n;\n}\n\n/*\n * A layer's picture: the one made nearest where the layer is now, and how\n * far it has scrolled since. A layer that has a\n+ * picture shows it: the picture's own bands, moved with the layer's scroll.\n+ * The picture is found by the layer's art key (bg_art_key), so it shows\n+ * whenever that layer does, on any visit to that screen.\n+ *\n+ * The picture's middle (the DS's own picture, 256 pixels of it) is not\n+ * drawn: the layer's own tiles are there already, and where the picture\n+ * says \"the game's own\" (its marker) the texel is transparent, so the\n+ * layer's own pixel shows through it. What the game draws past the DS's\n+ * edge (a map going on) is not drawn into the band: that is the port's own\n+ * rule's work (docs/PORTING.md, the wide screen), and it is not done yet.\n+ *\n+ * The wide canvas: 320 DS pixels, the DS's picture at x 32..287, the bands\n+ * at 0..31 and 288..319.\n+ */\n+\n+#define WIDE_CANVAS_W 320\n+#define WIDE_BAND_W 32\n+#define WIDE_ORIGIN 32 /* the DS's picture starts here */\n+\n+/* How far the layer may have scrolled from where the picture was made and\n+ * still show its bands (pokeplatinum-3ds's ART_REST). */\n+#define ART_REST 8\n+\n+/* One band: a rectangle of the picture's texture, at the canvas's x. */\n+static void put_band_quad(kj_v2d *v, int x, int y, int w, int h, int tx, int ty)\n+{\n+    const int16_t u0 = (int16_t)(tx * KJ_UV_UNIT + 1);\n+    const int16_t u1 = (int16_t)((tx + w) * KJ_UV_UNIT - 1);\n+    const int16_t v0 = (int16_t)(ty * KJ_UV_UNIT + 1);\n+    const int16_t v1 = (int16_t)((ty + h) * KJ_UV_UNIT - 1);\n+    v[0] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)x, (int16_t)y, u0, v0, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n+    v[1] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)(x + w), (int16_t)y, u1, v0, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n+    v[2] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)x, (int16_t)(y + h), u0, v1, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n+    v[3] = (kj_v2d){ (int16_t)(x + w), (int16_t)(y + h), u1, v1, 255, 255, 255, 255 };\n+}\n+\n+/*\n+ * The bands of a layer's picture, as quads. The picture's content is at\n+ * the canvas's x + dx (dx: how far the layer has scrolled since the\n+ * picture was made, to the right), so the picture's left band (its x 0..31)\n+ * is at the canvas's x -dx, and the canvas's band shows the picture's band\n+ * where they meet. What is left of the canvas's band is the picture's\n+ * middle: the game's own, which the layer draws itself.\n+ */\n+static void band_quads(const kj_wideart_pic *pic, int dx, drawable *out)\n+{\n+    uint32_t first;\n+    kj_v2d *v;\n+\n+    out->base = NULL;\n+    out->count = 0;\n+    v = kj_gpu_quads_alloc(2, &first);\n+    if (v == NULL) {\n+        return;\n+    }\n+    const int bh = pic->band_h;\n+    uint32_t n = 0;\n+\n+    /* the left band: the picture's x 0..31 */\n+    int lo = dx > 0 ? 0 : -dx;\n+    int hi = dx > 0 ? WIDE_BAND_W - dx : WIDE_BAND_W;\n+    if (hi > WIDE_BAND_W) {\n+        hi = WIDE_BAND_W;\n+    }\n+    if (hi > lo) {\n+        put_band_quad(v + n * 4u, lo - WIDE_ORIGIN, 0, hi - lo, bh, pic->left_x + (lo + dx), pic->left_y);\n+        ++n;\n+    }\n+\n+    /* the right band: the picture's x 288..319 */\n+    const int rx0 = WIDE_CANVAS_W - WIDE_BAND_W;\n+    lo = dx > 0 ? rx0 : rx0 - dx;\n+    hi = dx > 0 ? WIDE_CANVAS_W - dx : WIDE_CANVAS_W;\n+    if (hi > WIDE_CANVAS_W) {\n+        hi = WIDE_CANVAS_W;\n+    }\n+    if (hi > lo) {\n+        put_band_quad(v + n * 4u, lo - WIDE_ORIGIN, 0, hi - lo, bh, pic->right_x + (lo + dx - rx0),\n+                      pic->right_y);\n+        ++n;\n+    }\n+\n+    out->first = first;\n+    out->count = n;\n+}\n+\n+/*\n+ * A layer's picture: the one made nearest where the layer is now, and how\n+ * far it has scrolled since. The bands show while the layer is across from\n+ * where the picture was made (a few pixels either way); up and down doesn't\n+ * matter (a layer that bobs keeps its bands).\n+ */\n+static const kj_wideart_pic *layer_picture(const ctx *c, int bg, uint64_t key, int *dx_out)\n+{\n+    const uint16_t cnt = r16(c->regs, 0x08 + 2 * bg);\n+    const int map_w = s_text_sizes[cnt >> 14][0];\n+    const int map_h = s_text_sizes[cnt >> 14][1];\n+    const int cur_h = r16(c->regs, 0x10 + 4 * bg) & 0x1FF;\n+    const int cur_v = r16(c->regs, 0x12 + 4 * bg) & 0x1FF;\n+    const kj_wideart_pic *pic = kj_wideart_find_near(key, cur_h, cur_v, map_w, map_h, 256, 192, dx_out);\n+\n+    if (pic == NULL) {\n+        return NULL;\n+    }\n+    if (!(pic->flags & KJ_WIDE_ART_LOOP) && (*dx_out < -ART_REST || *dx_out > ART_REST)) {\n+        return NULL; /* the layer is elsewhere: nothing beyond the DS's edges */\n+    }\n+    return pic;\n+}\n+\n /* ------------------------------------------------------- retained layers */\n \n /*\n  * Retained layers (OPT-002/OPT-005).               "newString": "/* A text BG, retained when possible. */\nstatic bool text_bg_retained(const ctx *c, int bg, drawable *out, uint64_t *art_key)\n{\n    layer_cache *lc = &s_bg_cache[c->engine][bg];\n    const uint16_t *pal = pltt_ptr(c->in->mem, c->engine, 0);\n    uint8_t key[16];\n    uint32_t moff, mlen;\n\n    text_key(c, bg, key);\n    text_map_range(c, bg, &moff, &mlen);\n    const uint8_t *ext = text_ext_src(c, bg);\n    if (lc->valid && memcmp(lc->key, key, 16) == 0 && lc->map_off == moff && lc->map_len == mlen &&\n        memcmp(lc->pal, pal, 512) == 0 && memcmp(lc->map, c->bg_vram + moff, mlen) == 0 &&\n        lc->ext_src == ext && (ext == NULL || memcmp(lc->ext, ext, 0x2000) == 0) &&\n        chars_same(lc, c->bg_vram)) {\n        out->base = lc->quads;\n        out->count = lc->count;\n        *art_key = lc->art_key;\n#ifndef HGSS_PROFILE_OFF\n        ++s_reused_layers;\n#endif\n        return true;\n    }\n    if (!cache_alloc(lc)) {\n        return false;\n    }\n    run r;\n    memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));\n    r.ext = true;\n    r.v = lc->quads;\n    r.cap = CACHE_QUADS;\n    r.slots = lc->slots;\n    text_bg(c, bg, &r);\n    lc->valid = true;\n    memcpy(lc->key, key, 16);\n    memcpy(lc->pal, pal, 512);\n    lc->map_off = moff;\n    lc->map_len = mlen;\n    memcpy(lc->map, c->bg_vram + moff, mlen);\n    lc->ext_src = ext;\n    if (ext != NULL) {\n        memcpy(lc->ext, ext, 0x2000);\n    }\n    chars_keep(lc, c->bg_vram, r.char_lo, r.char_hi);\n    lc->count = r.count;\n    /* The art key is a hash of the same art the layer was built from, so it\n     * changes with it: it is worked out when the layer is built. */\n    lc->art_key = bg_art_key(c, bg);\n    *art_key = lc->art_key;\n    out->base = lc->quads;\n    out->count = r.count;\n    ++s_rebuilt_layers;\n    return true;\n}",

      "text": "<subagent sessionID=\"ses_e1a231742ffeHPx6QFOR6XsFUb\" state=\"completed\" description=\"Map p3ds lower-screen menu feature\">\n# The \"lower screen as a menu\" feature in `pokeplatinum-3ds` — technical specification\n\n*Prepared for the `sinjoh` engine (GPU-native, derived from kohjoh). Read-only analysis; nothing was edited, built or run.*\n\n---\n\n## 0. Scope: where the feature actually lives (the \"more files\" note)\n\nThe feature is **not** confined to `port_lowermenu.c` / `port_lowermap.c`. It is split across:\n\n**Port side (the engine you must satisfy):**\n\n| File | Role |\n|---|---|\n| `3ds_port/nitro/src/port_lowermenu.c` (77 KB) | The menu itself: the CPU-drawn 320×240 picture, the frame, the eight buttons + two squares, the small font, the tabs, the panel fade state machine, touch routing, press queue, and the map hand-over to the map drawer. |\n| `3ds_port/nitro/src/port_lowermap.c` / `.h` | The Town Map in the panel: reads `graphic/tmap_gra.narc` from the data pack, rasterises a 256×247 canvas on the CPU, reports dirty rows. |\n| `3ds_port/nitro/include/nitro_port_lowermenu.h` | **The public contract** (416 lines, exhaustively commented). |\n| `3ds_port/nitro/include/nitro_port_options.h` | The port's own settings (`NITRO_OPT_ITEM2` = the second square's item, `NITRO_OPT_START_TAB`). |\n| `3ds_port/nitro/src/port_render2d.c` + `include/nitro_port_render2d.h` | The \"tall\" picture: `NitroRender2DSplit.height` up to `NITRO_LOWERMENU_TALL_LINES` (248) so the lower screen's engine can be drawn past row 191. |\n| `3ds_port/game/app/port_compose_pica.c` (262 KB) | The 3DS compositor: draws the panel (three quads from the DS's picture texture, or the map's texture), the menu texture, the fade, the \"upper screen kept\" logic. |\n| `3ds_port/game/app/main_3ds.c` | The 3DS platform: routes touches to the menu, sets the tall split, starts the map drawer thread. |\n| `3ds_port/game/app/main_pc.c` | The PC runner: same contract (`mshot`/`cshot` screenshots), used as the reference for pixel-exactness. |\n| `3ds_port/nitro/tests/test_lowermenu.c` | ~80 behavioural checks of the contract (touch routing, presses, fade, panel runs, tabs). |\n\n**Game side (the patch series 0031–0041):** `src/start_menu.c` (the bulk), `src/overlay005/field_control.c`, `src/overlay005/ov5_021D5BC0.c`, `src/applications/town_map/{context.c,map_blocks.c}`, `src/applications/bag/{main.c,sprites.c,windows.c}`, `src/applications/party_menu/{main.c,sprites.c,windows.c,context_menu.c,form_change.c}`, `src/applications/pokemon_summary_screen/main.c`, `src/applications/trainer_case/main.c`, `src/overlay005/save_info_window.c`, `src/overlay005/script_message.c`, `src/overlay005/options_panel.c` (new file), `src/scrcmd.c`, `src/sprite_system.c`, `src/sprite_util.c`, `src/item_use_functions.c`, plus headers.\n\nThe **contract** the new engine must satisfy is exactly the `NitroPort_LowerMenu*` / `NitroPort_LowerMap*` API in `nitro_port_lowermenu.h` plus `port_lowermap.h`; everything else is game-side and can be reused verbatim.\n\n---\n\n## 1. What the feature is, from the user's side\n\n### 1.1 The shape of the screen\n\n`docs/REMASTER.md`, section **\"The lower screen as a menu\"** (line 1639):\n\n> \"In the field the lower screen is the port's menu, drawn at the 3DS's resolution (`port_lowermenu.c`, `include/nitro_port_lowermenu.h`): on the left a panel with the DS's lower screen in it (the Pokétch, or the Poké Ball before the player has one), at 15/16 of its size; on the right a column of eight buttons (MAP, POKéMON, BAG, TRAINER, POKéDEX, POKéTCH, SAVE, OPTIONS), each with its icon and name, over two squares for the registered items. Everywhere else (battles, the apps that take both screens) the lower screen is the DS's, filling the screen as before.\"\n\nAnd from `docs/REMASTER.md` line 14:\n\n> \"In the field the lower screen is a menu instead, with the DS's lower screen in a panel (see \"The lower screen as a menu\").\"\n\n`include/nitro_port_lowermenu.h` lines 1–21 states the layout contract:\n\n> \"In the field the lower screen is the port's own picture at the 3DS's resolution, 320 x 240: a panel on the left with the DS's lower screen in it at 15/16 of its size, and on the right a column of eight buttons (MAP, POKéMON, BAG, TRAINER, POKéDEX, POKéTCH, SAVE, OPTIONS) over two squares (the registered items).\"\n\nGeometry (`nitro_port_lowermenu.h` lines 31–46):\n\n* Menu picture: 320 × 240 (`NITRO_LOWERMENU_W/H`).\n* Panel: `NITRO_LOWERMENU_PANEL_X0 3`, `PANEL_Y0 4`, `PANEL_W 240`, `PANEL_H 232`.\n* Canvas: `NITRO_LOWERMENU_CANVAS_W 256`, `CANVAS_H 247`; the DS's 192 rows live at canvas rows `NITRO_LOWERMENU_DS_ROW0 27` … 27+191.\n* Button column: `port_lowermenu.c` lines 187–196: `BTN_X0 250`, `BTN_X1 316`, `BTN_Y(i) = 3 + 23*i`, `BTN_H 22`, icon box x 251–274, divider x 275, label x 277–314, red tab at x 317–318; the two item squares at `{250,197,282,229}` and `{285,197,317,229}`.\n* Tall mode: `NITRO_LOWERMENU_TALL_LINES 248` — the lower screen's 2D engine is drawn 248 lines tall so apps can put content below the DS's 192 rows.\n\n### 1.2 Panels that exist\n\n1. **The DS's lower screen** (the Pokétch in the field, the Poké Ball before the player has one) — drawn by the game's own 2D engine, shown in the panel at 15/16.\n2. **The Town Map** — the Town Map item's upper screen plus the guide page's description, drawn by the port from the ROM's own pictures.\n3. **The bag** (0035), **the party** (0037), **the summary** (0037), **the trainer case** (0038), **the save page** (0039), **the options page** (0040) — each rendered by the game onto the DS's lower screen (the \"DS's screen swap\") and shown in the panel, laid out tall (248 lines).\n\n### 1.3 Opening / closing\n\n* The Pokétch's handlers turn it on and off with the Pokétch's screen: patch **0031** hooks `ov5_021D5C4C` / `ov5_021D5C78` in `src/overlay005/ov5_021D5BC0.c` (`NitroPort_LowerMenuShow(TRUE/FALSE)`).\n* Only in the remaster display: `NitroPort_LowerMenuSetAvailable` is set by the platform (`port_compose_pica.c:1281`: `NitroPort_LowerMenuSetAvailable(sMenuTexData[0] != NULL)`; the PC runner sets `NitroPort_LowerMenuSetAvailable(!classicMenu)` at `main_pc.c:2347`). REMASTER: \"Only in the remaster display (the compositor says it can show it: `NitroPort_LowerMenuSetAvailable`, with the memory for its picture), and only without the 3D on the lower screen. In the classic display the game is the DS's.\"\n* **X** still opens the start menu, but the start menu *is* the lower menu in that case (0032): the start menu's window is never drawn and its sprites are hidden; the cursor lives on the lower menu's buttons.\n* **A tap on a button does what it says at once** (0036): \"A tap on a button does what it says at once, with the press's sound (the menu's opening sound is X's): the menu opens straight on it (its cursor on it from the start).\"\n* Leaving what the menu opened leaves the menu: \"Leaving what the menu opened (B, or the bag's button again; the party, the trainer card, the Pokédex, the options, the Town Map, the save's question answered no) leaves the menu too, back to walking, whether a tap or X opened it.\"\n* A double tap on MAP opens the Town Map app: \"A double tap on MAP (`NitroPort_LowerMenuPressDouble`: the second press on a button within half a second) opens the Town Map app; one tap only shows the map. A tap on the map does nothing.\"\n\n### 1.4 Which DS screens it replaces\n\nOnly **the field's lower screen**. In battles and in the apps that take both screens the lower screen is the DS's, filling the screen as before (REMASTER 1647–1648). The upper screen is untouched except when an app in the panel holds it (`NitroPort_LowerMenuHoldUpper`).\n\n---\n\n## 2. The game-side hooks, patch by patch\n\nThis is the contract the new engine must satisfy: the patches call **only** `NitroPort_LowerMenu*` / `NitroPort_LowerMap*` (plus a few unrelated port APIs: `NitroPort_Render2DSmoothObjs`, `NitroPort_Option`/`NitroPort_OptionSet`/`NitroPort_OptionsSave`, `NitroPort_WideLayout`).
